Search this repository very thoroughly for:

1. A webhook or HTTP callback system that notifies external systems when content changes. Look for outbound HTTP POST/request delivery functions related to webhooks, notifications, or event callbacks.
2. Any SSRF protection, URL validation, or mechanism that prevents webhook URLs from pointing at internal/private network addresses (e.g., checking for localhost, 127.0.0.1, 10.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x, private IPs, internal addresses).

Search for keywords like: webhook, callback, notify, hook, outbound, deliver, dispatch, ssrf, private, internal, localhost, reserved, loopback, isPrivate, validateURL, etc.

Search breadth: very thorough

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

60		tests := []struct {
61			name    string
62			secret  string
63			wantErr bool
64		}{
65			{name: "empty is allowed", secret: "", wantErr: false},
66			{name: "printable ascii", secret: "abcDEF123!@#", wantErr: false},
67			{name: "valid whsec_", secret: "whsec_" + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte("key")), wantErr: false},
68			{name: "newline rejected", secret: "abc\ndef", wantErr: true},

88	func TestPostSignsRequest(t *testing.T) {
89		// httptest listens on 127.0.0.1, which the SSRF guard blocks by default.
90		prev := AllowPrivateIPs

100			{name: "plain secret", secret: "plain-secret-value", key: []byte("plain-secret-value")},
101			{name: "whsec_ secret", secret: "whsec_" + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(rawKey), key: rawKey},
102		}

104		for _, tc := range cases {
105			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
106				var gotID, gotTimestamp, gotSignature string

108				server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
109					gotID = r.Header.Get("webhook-id")
110					gotTimestamp = r.Header.Get("webhook-timestamp")
111					gotSignature = r.Header.Get("webhook-signature")
112					gotBody, _ = io.ReadAll(r.Body)
113					_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"code":0}`))
114				}))
115				defer server.Close()
116	
117				err := Post(&WebhookRequestPayload{
118					URL:           server.URL,
119					ActivityType:  "memos.memo.created",
120					Creator:       "users/1",
121					SigningSecret: tc.secret,
122				})
123				require.NoError(t, err)
124	
125				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotID, "msg_"), "webhook-id should be prefixed with msg_")
126				require.NotEmpty(t, gotTimestamp)
127				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotSignature, "v1,"), "signature should carry the v1 version tag")
128	
129				// Recompute the signature the way a receiver would and confirm it matches.
130				mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, tc.key)
131				mac.Write([]byte(gotID + "." + gotTimestamp + "."))
132				mac.Write(gotBody)
133				want := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
134				require.Equal(t, "v1,"+want, gotSignature)
135			})
136		}
137	}
138	
139	// TestPostWithoutSecretSetsNoSignatureHeaders ensures unsigned webhooks stay unsigned.
140	func TestPostWithoutSecretSetsNoSignatureHeaders(t *testing.T) {
141		prev := AllowPrivateIPs
142		AllowPrivateIPs = true
143		defer func() { AllowPrivateIPs = prev }()
144	
145		var hasSignatureHeaders bool
146		server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
147			hasSignatureHeaders = r.Header.Get("webhook-id") != "" ||
148				r.Header.Get("webhook-timestamp") != "" ||
149				r.Header.Get("webhook-signature") != ""
150			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"code":0}`))
151		}))
152		defer server.Close()
153	
154		err := Post(&WebhookRequestPayload{
155			URL:          server.URL,
156			ActivityType: "memos.memo.created",
157			Creator:      "users/1",
158		})
159		require.NoError(t, err)
160		require.False(t, hasSignatureHeaders, "no signature headers should be set when no secret is configured")

---

## Findings

### 1. Webhook / HTTP Callback System

This repository (the "Memos" project) has a fully-featured webhook system that notifies external systems when content (memos) changes. Here are the key components:

**Core webhook dispatch engine:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go` -- Contains:
  - `Post()` (line 120): Synchronous outbound HTTP POST to a user-configured webhook URL. Marshals a `WebhookRequestPayload` to JSON, sends it via `safeClient`, and optionally signs the request body with HMAC-SHA256 using the Standard Webhooks protocol (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature` headers).
  - `PostAsync()` (line 184): Enqueues the payload onto a bounded channel (`asyncPostQueue`, capacity 128) for asynchronous dispatch by 4 background goroutines (lines 42-55).
  - `safeClient` (line 32): A dedicated `http.Client` whose transport uses `safeDialContext` for SSRF protection (see section 2).
  - `GenerateSigningSecret()` (line 111): Generates a `whsec_<base64>` signing secret backed by 32 random bytes.
  - `resolveSigningKey()` (line 97): Decodes `whsec_`-prefixed secrets from base64, or uses plain secrets as-is.

**Webhook payload structure** (`WebhookRequestPayload` at line 79):
  - `URL`, `ActivityType`, `Creator` (resource name), `Memo` (protobuf), `SigningSecret` (not serialized to JSON).

**Memo-triggered webhook dispatch:**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` -- Dispatch methods:
  - `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook()` (line 15) -- triggered from `memo_service.go` line 157
  - `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook()` (line 19) -- triggered from `memo_update_helpers.go` line 67
  - `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook()` (line 25) -- triggered from `memo_service.go` line 562
  - `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook()` (line 30) -- triggered from `memo_service_comments.go` line 119
  - All use `PostAsync()` for non-blocking delivery.

**Webhook CRUD API:**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go` -- Full CRUD:
  - `ListUserWebhooks()` (line 20)
  - `CreateUserWebhook()` (line 53) -- calls `webhook.ValidateURL()` on the URL at line 74, auto-generates signing secret if none supplied (line 82)
  - `UpdateUserWebhook()` (line 106) -- validates URL on update at lines 161 and 182
  - `DeleteUserWebhook()` (line 205)
  - `GetUserWebhookSigningSecret()` (line 253) -- owner-only endpoint to reveal the secret

**Storage layer:**
- `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` -- Webhooks stored as user settings:
  - `GetUserWebhooks()` (line 312)
  - `AddUserWebhook()` (line 329)
  - `RemoveUserWebhook()` (line 366)
  - `UpdateUserWebhook()` (line 393)

**Proto definitions:**
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/user_setting.proto` -- `WebhooksUserSetting` message (line 123)
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` -- `UserWebhook` message (line 696), RPC endpoints (lines 143-177)

**Frontend:**
- `/bench/repo/web/src/components/Settings/WebhookSection.tsx` -- Settings UI for listing, creating, editing, deleting webhooks
- `/bench/repo/web/src/components/CreateWebhookDialog.tsx` -- Create/edit dialog with signing secret reveal/generate

---

### 2. SSRF Protection / URL Validation

The repository has **two independent SSRF protection systems** -- one for the webhook subsystem and one for the HTTP metadata getter. Both follow the same pattern of blocking private/reserved IPs at dial time.

#### A. Webhook SSRF Protection (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go` and `webhook.go`)

**Validation at registration time** (`ValidateURL()`, validate.go line 62):
1. Parses the URL and rejects non-http/https schemes (line 67-69)
2. Resolves the hostname via DNS (`net.LookupHost`) (line 71)
3. Checks every resolved IP against `isReservedIP()` (line 78)
4. Returns a gRPC `InvalidArgument` error if any IP is reserved

**Validation at dispatch time** (`safeDialContext()`, webhook.go line 59):
1. Resolves the hostname again at connection time (line 65) -- this defeats DNS rebinding attacks where a hostname resolves to a public IP at registration time but to a private IP later
2. Checks all resolved IPs against `isReservedIP()` (line 71)
3. Rejects the connection if any IP is reserved

**Reserved IP ranges** (validate.go lines 14-23):
- `127.0.0.0/8` -- IPv4 loopback
- `10.0.0.0/8` -- RFC-1918 class A
- `172.16.0.0/12` -- RFC-1918 class B
- `192.168.0.0/16` -- RFC-1918 class C
- `169.254.0.0/16` -- Link-local (includes cloud IMDS at 169.254.169.254)
- `::1/128` -- IPv6 loopback
- `fc00::/7` -- IPv6 unique local
- `fe80::/10` -- IPv6 link-local

**Escape hatch** (`AllowPrivateIPs`, validate.go line 41):
- A package-level boolean that, when set to `true`, disables the SSRF protection entirely. Described as useful for self-hosted deployments targeting local network services. Currently only set to `true` in test code (webhook_test.go lines 91 and 142).

#### B. HTTP Getter SSRF Protection (`/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go`)

This is a separate protection system for the link preview / HTML metadata fetcher:

**`secureDialContext()`** (line 51): Same pattern -- resolves hostname, calls `resolveAllowedIPs()` which calls `isInternalIP()`.

**`isInternalIP()`** (line 104): Uses Go's built-in IP classification methods:
- `ip.IsLoopback()` -- 127.x.x.x, ::1
- `ip.IsPrivate()` -- 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, fc00::/7
- `ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast()` -- 169.254.x, fe80::/10
- `ip.IsUnspecified()` -- 0.0.0.0, ::

**`validateURL()`** (line 108): Validates scheme (http/https only), checks for literal private IP addresses in the URL.

**Redirect protection** (`newHTTPClient()`, line 31): The HTTP client's `CheckRedirect` function (line 39-45) re-validates the redirect target URL against `validateURL()`, preventing redirect-based SSRF bypass.

**`GetImage()` at `/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/image.go` line 21**: This function uses bare `http.Get()` (the default HTTP client) WITHOUT SSRF protection. This is a notable difference from `GetHTMLMeta()` which uses the protected `httpClient`.

---

### Summary

The webhook system is well-protected against SSRF with a defense-in-depth approach:
- URL validation at webhook registration (create and update)
- IP validation at dial time (protects against DNS rebinding)
- Comprehensive coverage of reserved ranges (IPv4 and IPv6, including cloud IMDS)
- HTTP/HTTPS scheme enforcement

One notable finding: `/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/image.go` line 21 uses `http.Get()` (Go's default client) without SSRF protection, unlike the HTML meta getter which uses the protected `httpClient` with `secureDialContext`. This could be an SSRF vector if `GetImage()` is called with user-controlled URLs.
